verdict.rationale: Neon supports bulk/programmatic operations mainly at the infrastructure level — the Management API and MCP server expose project/branch lifecycle operations (create/delete/restore) and Neon explicitly documents managing 'tens of thousands (in some cases, millions) of projects programmatically through the Neon API' for project-per-user platforms, plus scoped API keys for automation. However, there is no evidence of bulk operations on data/rows within a database (e.g., batch SQL execution across many records/tables in one call beyond standard SQL, or a dedicated bulk-import/bulk-update tool) — the MCP tools are largely single-item (create/restore/delete one project/branch at a time) rather than an explicit multi-item batch primitive. missing for 10: evidence of a dedicated bulk/batch API endpoint or MCP tool operating on many items in a single call, and independent/hands-on confirmation of bulk operations at scale beyond vendor docs.
